title: Autoscaler signal fusion and probe alignment postmortem
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: During a high-traffic experiment on 2026-02-27 we observed repeated autoscaler oscillations that caused a sustained period of underprovisioning for gen-inference pools. The event lasted ~3 hours, causing 5–15% request latency tail increases and several customer errors for latency-sensitive endpoints. This ticket documents the diagnosis, immediate mitigations, root cause, and follow-up action items to prevent signal-misalignment and double-counting in the autoscaling stack.
timeline: 2026-02-27T09:14Z - First pager: observed 95th percentile request latency spike for gen-inference-prod-route-12 (alert autoscale-latency-95).
2026-02-27T09:22Z - Oncall rotated probes and confirmed KEDA scaled down two replicas within 30s of a CPU-surge subsiding.
2026-02-27T09:35Z - Multiple scale-downs followed by rapid scale-ups as QPS and queue-latency signals oscillated; warm-pool empty for that cohort.
2026-02-27T10:01Z - Engineering lead assigned and mitigation plan enacted: temporarily increase minReplicas and pulse a warm pre-warm job.
2026-02-27T11:45Z - Traffic normalized after pre-warm completed and scale hysteresis window extended. Post-incident monitoring started.
2026-02-27T12:30Z - Incident declared over; postmortem investigation initiated and logs/metrics archived to S3.
analysis: Multiple telemetry sources (CPU, user-facing P95 latency, queue length) were fed independently into a hybrid HPA+KEDA control loop without time-alignment or de-duplication, causing the controller to see multiple overlapping ‘spikes’ for the same workload burst.
KEDA scaler and HPA were both configured to react to slightly different metric windows (KEDA: 30s EMA, HPA: 60s P95) which caused mismatched decisions during rapid load changes.

Probe jitter: readiness probe failures from newly started replicas were interpreted as elevated failure rates by a synthetic SLO probe, increasing perceived customer impact and prompting aggressive upscales.
Warm pool depletion: we lack a fast replenishment path for specific model families; pre-warm tasks were queued behind lower-priority jobs causing additional cold-start exposure.
Rate-limited control-plane writes: during the scale flapping we hit our rate limit for autoscaler updates which introduced additional lag and made hysteresis ineffective.
root_cause: A combination of signal misalignment (mismatched windows and semantics between KEDA and HPA), unfiltered duplicate telemetry (same underlying burst surfaced by CPU, queue, and SLO probes), and an underprovisioned warm-pool replenishment path caused the autoscaling control loop to oscillate. Secondary contributor: control-plane write throttling delayed corrective scaling operations.
mitigation_taken: Raised minReplicas for impacted pools to short-term safe floor (3 -> 6) to avoid immediate underprovisioning.
Triggered manual pre-warm job to populate warm-pool for the affected model family (runtime-gen-large).
Extended KEDA and HPA decision windows and added a temporary 45s stabilization window to reduce reaction sensitivity.
Increased autoscaler API write quota temporarily to prevent throttling during recovery.
action_items: AF-1: Implement a signal-fusion layer in the autoscaler to deduplicate correlated signals and compute a single scale decision input. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-04-07.
AF-2: Align KEDA/HPA metric windows and document canonical metric semantics for each scaler type (contribution: runtime-team + autoscale-team). Owner: Mei Chen. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-24.
AF-3: Add a decay-weighted cross-signal matcher to avoid double-counting the same burst across CPU/queue/latency probes. Owner: Andre Silva. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-04-14.
AF-4: Build a prioritized warm-pool replenisher so pre-warm jobs for latency-sensitive model families can jump the queue. Owner: Josefa Alvarez. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-04-01.
AF-5: Instrument and publish a new autoscaler dashboard showing fused-signal value, raw inputs, and decision timeline for each scale event. Owner: Analytics. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-17.
AF-6: Add automatic rate-limit backoff/retry logic to autoscaler control-plane writes and a reactive circuit breaker to avoid delayed hysteresis. Owner: Platform Core. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-31.
AF-7: Run a canary with synthetic bursts across model families to validate fusion heuristics and warm-pool replenisher under controlled load. Owner: SRE. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-04-10.
follow_up_experiments: Experiment E-01: Compare 3 fusion strategies (max-rule, weighted-average with decay, and voting) on historical trace replay for the last 6 months.
Experiment E-02: Synthetic burst test to measure TTFP (time-to-first-product) with and without prioritized replenisher across top 5 models.
Experiment E-03: Throttle autoscaler write path in staging to validate exponential-backoff and circuit-breaker behavior.
notes: We should avoid overfitting fusion heuristics to a single model family; experiments must include a diverse set of workloads (chat, embedding, rerank).
Consider making signal-fusion configurable per-customer for Dedicated customers who prefer different sensitivity trade-offs.
Cross-team coordination: platform-core will prioritize API write robustness while runtime team owns warm-pool replenisher behavior.
